sources.name: Game values
sources.note: Event effects, weights and check thresholds are simplified game values.

events.title: Problem during launch
events.text: One rocket engine stops too early on the way up. The computer has only seconds to make a new plan.
events.debriefPrepared: Your Backup Computer made a quick new plan when the launch went wrong.
events.debriefUnprepared: You had no Backup Computer, so the launch problem cost you safety or fuel.

choices.label: Let the computer make a new plan
choices.outcome: With only one computer, the new plan was slow. The long engine burn shook the spacecraft and used extra fuel.
choices.preparedOutcome: The Backup Computer made a new plan in less than a second. This is how modern rockets survive when an engine stops.

choices.label: Stop in a lower orbit, then climb back up
choices.outcome: You saved the spacecraft. But climbing back to the right orbit used your own fuel.

events.source: Game scenario: engine-out during ascent. Its chance grows as the launch vehicle's reliability falls.

events.title: Nuclear safety review
events.text: People are worried about launching a nuclear reactor. So there is an extra safety review just before launch.
events.debriefUnprepared: You chose a Nuclear engine, so your mission needed an extra safety review.

choices.label: Wait for a full public review
choices.outcome: The review cost time and money. But public trust is important for nuclear missions.

choices.label: Pay for extra safety and launch on time
choices.outcome: The extra safety tests were expensive. Rushing also added a little risk.

events.source: Game scenario: nuclear launches go through extra safety and public review.

events.title: Solar flare!
events.text: Scientists see a huge burst of energy from the Sun. A storm of radiation will reach you in less than an hour.
events.debriefPrepared: Strong radiation protection kept you safe from the solar flare.
events.debriefUnprepared: The solar flare hurt you. More radiation protection would make it weaker.

choices.label: Point your shield at the Sun
choices.outcome: Your protection was too weak. Radiation got through and hit the spacecraft.
choices.preparedOutcome: Your strong protection stopped the radiation storm.

choices.label: Turn off the instruments and wait
choices.outcome: Turning things off protected the electronics. But you lost science time, and some radiation still got through.
choices.preparedOutcome: With good protection, you only needed to turn things off for a short time.

events.source: Inspired by NASA DONKI space-weather records of solar flares (FLR) and solar energetic particle (SEP) events.

events.title: Radiation is building up
events.text: On this long trip, cosmic rays keep hitting the crew. Cosmic rays are tiny particles from exploding stars far away.
events.checkLabel: A Habitat (its water and food also block radiation)
events.debriefPrepared: The water and food in your Habitat also blocked cosmic rays.
events.debriefUnprepared: Your crew flew through deep space with no Radiation Shield. They got more radiation.

choices.label: Build a shelter from water and food
choices.outcome: Water blocks radiation well. But you did not have much water.
choices.preparedOutcome: The water tanks in your Habitat made a very good shelter.

choices.label: Use extra fuel to fly faster
choices.outcome: Less time in deep space means less radiation. But it cost fuel.

events.source: Space-radiation exposure reasoning informed by NASA OSDR (incl. RadLab) data.

events.title: Hit by space dust
events.text: A tiny piece of space dust hits you at about 20 km/s. It goes through the outer wall and damages the flight computer.
events.debriefPrepared: Your Backup Computer took over after the space dust hit.
events.debriefUnprepared: You had no Backup Computer, so one hit from space dust hurt your safety.

choices.label: Switch to backup and keep flying
choices.outcome: You had no real backup. You flew on with damaged electronics.
choices.preparedOutcome: The Backup Computer took over at once.

choices.label: Stop and check everything
choices.outcome: The checks took days, and the damage still hurt.
choices.preparedOutcome: The checks showed that the Backup Computer works well.

events.source: NASA Orbital Debris Program Office: micrometeoroid and debris environment.

events.title: Radio contact lost
events.text: The Sun moves between Earth and your spacecraft. Noise from the Sun blocks your radio signal.
events.debriefPrepared: Your Big Antenna kept in contact with Earth.
events.debriefUnprepared: Your weak radio lost contact with Earth.

choices.label: Stay where you are and wait for contact
choices.outcome: Your weak radio needed a long wait. Your science data could not be sent.
choices.preparedOutcome: Your Big Antenna got through the noise again in a few days.

choices.label: Fly on autopilot until contact comes back
choices.outcome: Without help from Earth, you flew a little in the wrong direction.
choices.preparedOutcome: Good contact before and after kept the autopilot on the right path.

events.source: Game scenario based on how Mars missions pause commanding during solar conjunction.

events.title: A part broke
events.text: A reaction wheel stops working. This spinning wheel turns the spacecraft to face the right way.
events.checkLabel: A Spare Parts Kit on board
events.debriefPrepared: You had a Spare Parts Kit, so the broken part was quick to fix.
events.debriefUnprepared: You had no spare parts, so the broken part cost you a lot.

choices.label: Fix the wheel
choices.outcome: With no spare parts, the repair took days and did not fully work.
choices.preparedOutcome: The kit had a new wheel. You changed it quickly.

choices.label: Turn the spacecraft with small rocket jets
choices.outcome: Small rocket jets can turn the spacecraft, but they use fuel. NASA's Dawn spacecraft did this after its wheels broke.

events.source: Reaction-wheel failures happened on NASA's Dawn and Kepler missions.

events.title: An astronaut is sick
events.text: An astronaut has a fever and feels dizzy. A doctor on Earth can help by radio.
events.debriefPrepared: Good crew care, with a medical room and supplies, helped the sick astronaut.
events.debriefUnprepared: With little crew care, a simple illness became dangerous.

choices.label: Treat the astronaut on board
choices.outcome: You had few medical supplies. The astronaut got better slowly, and it was risky.
choices.preparedOutcome: The medical room had everything needed. The astronaut was back at work in a few days.

choices.label: End the mission early
choices.outcome: Everyone came home sooner. But you lost some of the planned science.

events.source: Game scenario based on crew health planning for long missions.

events.title: Danger at the landing site
events.text: As you come down to land, the camera shows big rocks. The map showed flat ground.
events.debriefPrepared: Your spare fuel let you fly past the big rocks, like Apollo 11 did.
events.debriefUnprepared: You had little spare fuel, so you could not fly around the danger.

choices.label: Fly to a safer place
choices.outcome: Flying to a new place used a lot of fuel. With little spare fuel, this was risky.
choices.preparedOutcome: You had plenty of spare fuel. You flew past the rocks and landed gently.

choices.label: Land carefully where you are
choices.outcome: One leg landed on a rock. The lander leaned over, and some equipment broke.

events.source: Apollo 11's descent: Neil Armstrong flew past a boulder field with little fuel to spare.

events.title: Huge dust storm
events.text: Dust covers the sky over all of Mars. For weeks, solar panels will make only a little power.
events.checkLabel: Spare power in a storm: 0 kW or more. A Nuclear Battery and Extra Batteries help.
events.debriefPrepared: Steady power from a Nuclear Battery or batteries kept you going in the dust storm.
events.debriefUnprepared: You had little spare power, so the dust storm was dangerous. NASA lost the Opportunity rover this way in 2018.

choices.label: Sleep until the sky is clear
choices.outcome: There was not enough power for the heaters. The cold damaged some equipment.
choices.preparedOutcome: Your power kept the heaters on. You waited a short time, then continued.

choices.label: Keep working with little power
choices.outcome: You got a little science. But the batteries became dangerously low.
choices.preparedOutcome: With steady power, you could study the storm. That is a rare chance.

events.source: NASA's Opportunity rover fell silent during the 2018 global dust storm on Mars.

events.title: A chance to discover something
events.text: Your instruments see something new nearby: a young crater with bright material inside.
events.checkLabel: HD Cameras or a Rock Scanner on board
events.debriefPrepared: Your instruments turned a lucky find into extra science.
events.debriefUnprepared: You did not have the right instruments for this discovery.

choices.label: Go and look (uses fuel and time)
choices.outcome: Without the right instruments, you got only a little data.
choices.preparedOutcome: Your instruments found out what the material is. A big discovery!

choices.label: Keep to the plan
choices.outcome: You saved your fuel and time for the rest of the mission.

events.source: Game scenario: unplanned discoveries reward the right instruments and spare fuel.

events.title: The sampler sinks into Bennu
events.text: The sample arm touches Bennu and keeps going down. The ground is only loose small rocks, like a pool full of balls.
events.checkLabel: A Sample Return Capsule on board
events.debriefPrepared: Your Sample Return Capsule kept a big sample from Bennu's surprising surface.
events.debriefUnprepared: You had no Sample Return Capsule, so you got little from Bennu.

choices.label: Take as much as you can
choices.outcome: You had no safe place to keep it. You lost most of the sample.
choices.preparedOutcome: The capsule kept a big sample, like NASA's OSIRIS-REx did in 2020.

choices.label: Move away at once
choices.outcome: A quick engine burn moved you away safely. But the sample was small.

events.source: NASA OSIRIS-REx touch-and-go sample collection at Bennu, October 2020.
